claim: Python was conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum.
label: SUPPORTS
evidence: Python was conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum at Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) in the Netherlands.

claim: Python was released initially in the year 2010.
label: REFUTES
evidence: Python was first released in 1991 as Python 0.9.0, followed by Python 2.0 in 2000 and Python 3.0 in 2008.

claim: Guido van Rossum won an Olympic gold medal for swimming in 1992.
label: NOT ENOUGH INFO
evidence: Guido van Rossum is a Dutch programmer best known as the creator of the Python programming language.

claim: Retrieval-Augmented Generation was introduced by Patrick Lewis and colleagues in 2020.
label: SUPPORTS
evidence: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks was published by Patrick Lewis et al. at NeurIPS 2020.

claim: BM25 is a machine learning deep neural network architecture.
label: REFUTES
evidence: BM25 is a probabilistic lexical ranking function based on the bag-of-words retrieval model, not a neural network.

claim: The BM25 algorithm was developed during a chess tournament in Iceland.
label: NOT ENOUGH INFO
evidence: BM25 was developed by Stephen Robertson, Karen Spärck Jones, and colleagues in the 1970s and 1980s for text retrieval.

claim: FAISS was developed by Facebook AI Research for efficient vector similarity search.
label: SUPPORTS
evidence: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is a library developed by Facebook AI Research for efficient similarity search of dense vectors.

claim: FAISS requires quantum computers to execute nearest neighbor lookups.
label: REFUTES
evidence: FAISS is written in C++ with Python wrappers and executes on standard CPU and GPU hardware.

claim: Sentence Transformers models produce continuous vector embeddings for text sequences.
label: SUPPORTS
evidence: Sentence-BERT and Sentence Transformers use siamese BERT networks to derive semantically meaningful sentence embeddings.

claim: All Sentence Transformers embedding models require exactly 128 gigabytes of RAM to run.
label: NOT ENOUGH INFO
evidence: Sentence Transformers provides various model sizes ranging from lightweight MiniLM models to large transformer architectures.
